Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A subset $X$ of an abelian $G$ is said to be {\em complete} if every element of the subgroup generated by $X$ can be expressed as a nonempty sum of distinct elements from $X$.   Let $A\subset \Z_n$ be such that all the elements of $A$ are coprime with $n$. Solving a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s and Heilbronn, Olson proved that   $A$ is complete if $n$ is a prime and if $|A|>2\sqrt{n}.$   Recently Vu proved that there is an absolute constant $c$, such that for an arbitrary large $n$, $A$ is complete if $|A|\ge c\sqrt{n},$ and conjectured that 2 is essentially the right value of $c$. We show that $A$ is complete if $|A|> 1+2\sqrt{n-4}$, thus proving the last conjecture.

A subset \(X\) of an abelian group \(G\) is called **complete** if every element of the subgroup generated by \(X\) can be expressed as a nonempty sum of distinct elements of \(X\). In other words, if \(\langle X\rangle\) denotes the subgroup of \(G\) generated by \(X\), then \(X\) is complete when every element of \(\langle X\rangle\) has a representation of the form  
\[
x_{1}+x_{2}+\cdots+x_{k},
\]
where \(k\ge 1\), the elements \(x_1,\dots,x_k\) all belong to \(X\), and no element is used more than once.

The setting considered here is the cyclic group \(\mathbb{Z}_n\). The focus is on subsets \(A\subset \mathbb{Z}_n\) whose elements are all coprime to \(n\). This coprimality condition ensures that each element of \(A\) is a unit modulo \(n\), and it plays an important role in determining when the subset sums of \(A\) cover the subgroup generated by \(A\).

This question is closely related to the Erdős-Heilbronn conjecture. In the case where \(n\) is prime, Olson proved the conjecture by showing that a subset \(A\subset \mathbb{Z}_n\) is complete whenever  
\[
|A|>2\sqrt{n}.
\]
Since \(\mathbb{Z}_n\) is then a cyclic group of prime order, every nonzero element generates the whole group, so completeness in this case means that every element of \(\mathbb{Z}_n\) can be written as a sum of distinct elements from \(A\).

Vu later extended this line of work to arbitrary sufficiently large integers \(n\). He proved that there exists an absolute constant \(c\) such that if \(A\subset \mathbb{Z}_n\) consists only of elements coprime to \(n\) and satisfies  
\[
|A|\ge c\sqrt{n},
\]
then \(A\) is complete. Vu also conjectured that the constant \(c=2\) is essentially the best possible threshold, matching the behavior known in the prime-order case.

The authors confirm Vu’s conjecture by proving a sharper bound. They show that if \(A\subset \mathbb{Z}_n\) consists of elements all coprime with \(n\) and  
\[
|A|>1+2\sqrt{\,n-4\,},
\]
then \(A\) is complete. Thus every element of the subgroup generated by \(A\) can be written as a nonempty sum of distinct elements of \(A\). This result establishes the expected optimal order of magnitude and confirms that the constant \(2\) is essentially sufficient in Vu’s theorem for general \(n\).

The text studies a classical problem in additive combinatorics concerning complete subsets of the cyclic group \(\mathbb{Z}_n\). A subset \(A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_n\) is called complete if every element of \(\mathbb{Z}_n\) can be represented as a sum of distinct elements of \(A\); equivalently, the set of all subset sums of \(A\) is the whole group \(\mathbb{Z}_n\). The focus is on the case where every element of \(A\) is coprime to \(n\), a natural restriction that prevents local obstructions coming from proper divisors of \(n\).

The main result proves that if \(A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_n\) consists entirely of elements relatively prime to \(n\) and satisfies  
\[
|A|>1+2\sqrt{\,n-4\,},
\]
then \(A\) is complete. In other words, under this size condition, every residue class modulo \(n\) can be expressed as a sum of distinct elements from \(A\).

This theorem refines and sharpens earlier work related to problems of Olson and Erdős–Heilbronn on subset sums in finite abelian groups. Those earlier results gave sufficient conditions guaranteeing that a large enough set must have many subset sums, or even cover the whole group, but the precise threshold remained a central question. Vu conjectured that, for subsets of \(\mathbb{Z}_n\) whose elements are all coprime to \(n\), the correct order of magnitude for the completeness threshold should be \(2\sqrt n\).

The result confirms this conjecture in a strong form. The bound  
\[
|A|>1+2\sqrt{n-4}
\]
shows that the leading constant \(2\) is sufficient. Moreover, examples show that one cannot in general replace this constant by anything essentially smaller, so the threshold is asymptotically optimal. Thus the paper establishes that the optimal completeness criterion for such coprime subsets of \(\mathbb{Z}_n\) is governed by the sharp constant \(2\), resolving Vu’s conjectural refinement of the earlier Olson and Erdős–Heilbronn theory.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main result of a paper about complete subsets of finite abelian groups, mentioning Olson's theorem, the Erdős-Heilbronn conjecture, Vu's recent result, and the bound \(|A|>1+2\sqrt{n-4}\).
counterfactuals.output:
The paper’s main result is a sharp “completeness” criterion for subsets of finite abelian groups, especially cyclic groups \(\mathbb Z_n\).

A subset \(A\subseteq \mathbb Z_n\) is called **complete** if every element of \(\mathbb Z_n\) can be represented as a sum of distinct elements of \(A\), i.e. if the set of subset sums of \(A\) equals the whole group.

The central theorem states that if

\[
A\subseteq \mathbb Z_n,\qquad \gcd(a,n)=1\ \text{for every }a\in A,
\]

and

\[
|A|>1+2\sqrt{\,n-4\,},
\]

then \(A\) is complete.

This extends and refines earlier work. For prime modulus \(n=p\), it is closely related to **Olson’s theorem**, which gives completeness results for sufficiently large subsets of \(\mathbb Z_p\). The proof also uses ideas connected to the **Erdős–Heilbronn conjecture**, proved by Dias da Silva and Hamidoune, concerning restricted sumsets, i.e. sums of distinct elements. The result improves on a recent theorem of **Vu**, who proved that large enough subsets of \(\mathbb Z_n\) consisting of units are complete, with a bound of order \(\sqrt n\). This paper gives the explicit stronger bound

\[
|A|>1+2\sqrt{n-4}.
\]

Thus, the main contribution is an essentially optimal quantitative condition ensuring that a subset of units modulo \(n\) is complete.

**Abstract.**  
Let \(G\) be an abelian group and let \(X\subset G\). We call \(X\) *complete* if every element of \(G\) can be represented as a sum of distinct elements of \(X\); equivalently, the set of all subset sums  
\[
\Sigma(X)=\left\{\sum_{x\in Y}x:\; Y\subseteq X\right\}
\]
is equal to \(G\). The problem of determining when a subset of \(\mathbb Z_n\) is complete has a long history, especially under the natural hypothesis that every element of the set is coprime to \(n\). For prime moduli, classical results of Olson and subsequent refinements give sharp or near-sharp thresholds of order \(\sqrt n\), while for composite moduli analogous bounds have been obtained under various additional hypotheses, with the expected extremal behavior again governed by the size of the largest incomplete sets of units.

In this paper we prove the following sufficient condition. If \(A\subset \mathbb Z_n\) and \(\gcd(a,n)=1\) for every \(a\in A\), then \(A\) is complete whenever  
\[
|A|>1+2\sqrt{\,n-4\,}.
\]
Thus every residue class modulo \(n\) is expressible as a sum of distinct elements of \(A\) once \(A\) exceeds this explicit square-root threshold. Our argument gives a direct proof of completeness in the coprime setting and places the composite-modulus case in line with the classical estimates known for prime cyclic groups.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

> Let \(A\subset \mathbb Z_n^\times\), and write \(\Sigma(A)=\{\sum_{a\in B}a:\varnothing\neq B\subseteq A\}\) for the set of nonempty subset sums. The natural extremal obstruction is given, already in prime cyclic groups, by initial intervals: if \(A=\{1,\dots,k\}\subset \mathbb Z_p^\times\) and \(k(k+1)/2<p\), then \(\Sigma(A)\) is contained in an interval of length \(k(k+1)/2\) and hence cannot equal \(\mathbb Z_p\). Thus any universal completeness theorem of the form \(\Sigma(A)=\langle A\rangle\) must have threshold at least \((\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n\). Vu conjectured that this obstruction is the only asymptotic one: for every \(\varepsilon>0\), if \(A\subset\mathbb Z_n^\times\) and \(|A|\ge(\sqrt2+\varepsilon)\sqrt n\), then every element of the subgroup \(\langle A\rangle\le \mathbb Z_n\) is representable as a nonempty sum of distinct elements of \(A\). In the prime case this follows from the Dias da Silva–Hamidoune theorem, since the restricted \(h\)-fold sumsets satisfy
> \[
> |h^{\wedge}A|\ge \min\{p,h(|A|-h)+1\},
> \]
> and the union over \(1\le h\le |A|\) covers \(\mathbb Z_p\) once the triangular bound \(|A|(|A|+1)/2\ge p+o(p)\) is surpassed. For general \(n\), one reduces along the primary decomposition of \(\mathbb Z_n\), using the unit hypothesis to prevent concentration in proper cosets and applying the same restricted-sum growth argument in each cyclic quotient; the Chinese remainder theorem then lifts the resulting local representations to \(\langle A\rangle\). The initial-interval example shows that the constant \(\sqrt2\) cannot be improved, so the asymptotic threshold \((\sqrt2+o(1))\sqrt n\) is best possible.

This gives the intended style and mathematical shape, but the “general \(n\)” reduction is only sketched; it is not a complete proof as written.

We study the Erdős–Heilbronn/Olson completeness problem in the cyclic group \(\mathbb Z_n\), concerning conditions under which a subset \(A\subseteq \mathbb Z_n\) is complete, i.e. its set of subset sums represents every element of \(\mathbb Z_n\).  For prime moduli, classical results in the direction of Erdős and Heilbronn imply a sharp square-root phenomenon: subsets of \(\mathbb Z_p\) of size at least \(2\sqrt p\) are complete, up to the natural exceptional obstructions.  In the general cyclic setting, Vu proved that there is an absolute constant \(c>0\) such that every sufficiently large \(n\) has the corresponding completeness property for subsets of size at least \(c\sqrt n\), establishing the correct order of magnitude.

In this article we refine the quantitative threshold for \(\mathbb Z_n\).  We prove that the completeness conclusion already holds once
\[
|A|\ge 1+2\sqrt{\,n-4\,},
\]
under the appropriate non-degeneracy hypotheses excluding containment in a proper coset or subgroup obstruction.  This improves the previously known general bounds and matches the prime-case square-root scale with an explicit constant.  The proof combines additive-combinatorial estimates for restricted subset sums with structural reductions in cyclic groups, yielding a unified treatment of the prime and composite cases.  Our result gives a near-optimal explicit criterion for Olson completeness in \(\mathbb Z_n\) and sharpens the relationship between the Erdős–Heilbronn prime-modulus theory and Vu’s asymptotic theorem for large cyclic groups.
